findings.title: Ordinary handlers lack a bound on multiple committed effects
findings.impact: A successful provider call followed by a proved no-effect failure cannot justify retrying the whole handler; committed local work before or required work after dispatch has the same partial-progress problem.
findings.suggestedFix: Admit one local atomic unit or one reviewed external-dispatch protocol; transitively reject other mixed/multiple-effect paths until E08 specifies recorded step outcomes and resumption.
findings.correction: Bounded handler recovery section, compiler/runtime plan and EV-16.

findings.title: Ordering lane identity must survive handler and version changes
findings.impact: Mapping delivery job identity to each handler/version would let later selectors or builds overtake an unresolved earlier event for the same subscriber/aggregate.
findings.suggestedFix: Use stable application/tenant/subscriber plus typed aggregate or one subscriber-wide fallback lane; preserve predecessor order across versions and require a barrier for key changes.
findings.correction: Defaults and ordering section, runtime plan and EV-17.

findings.title: A causal delivery needs separate producer and executor builds
findings.impact: An event emitted by build A may fail in compatible handler build B; a single manifest reference misattributes one endpoint.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve immutable producer manifest/site in the event and actual execution manifest/site per attempt, separately from the enrolled handler contract version.
findings.correction: Event envelope, incident lookup, E11 plan and EV-15/identity proof matrix.

findings.title: Examples use reserved event keyword as a payload binding
findings.impact: The declaration keyword is hard-reserved; canonical examples otherwise require an unintended contextual exception.
findings.suggestedFix: Use payload consistently and add binding/reference keyword-negative cases.
findings.correction: Event and syntax examples, grammar constraints and EV-18.

findings.title: Delegated authority intersection was conditional and omitted worker invoke
findings.impact: Origin permission could substitute for worker permission on downstream emission, or the qualifier could admit worker-only resource effects.
findings.correction: Require unconditional worker-and-origin permissions on ordinary protected reads/mutations/emissions; fail closed for absent origin and allow differences only in named qualified protocols.

findings.title: Use existing Unit no-result type
findings.impact: None would add an undefined second no-result type to the statement rule.
findings.correction: Emission, handler completion and standalone admitted calls use Unit; nullable none remains distinct.

findings.title: Intrinsic emission acknowledgement was underspecified
findings.impact: Optional attempt could accept bare emission when it has only operational faults; direct intrinsic matching had no defined outcome API.
findings.correction: Require attempt on every emit_event expression/statement and reject direct intrinsic matching; ordinary Unit calls retain existing exact-failure rules.

findings.correction: Checked projection declaration/IR plus exact protected approval binding; ordinary projection writes and name-based activation forbidden; explicit CONSISTENCY-001/RM-405–RM-407 reuse without conditional activation.

findings.title: Future enrollment does not establish complete projection coverage
findings.correction: Partial coverage since explicit generation; absence means not observed; complete lists/counts require separately authorised consistent bootstrap and catch-up barrier; coverage separate from lag.

findings.correction: Read and aggregate binding covers app/tenant, nominal source identity, source incarnation and compatible active projection generation before current policy/lifecycle; no current-revision equality requirement; EV-24 old-row/new-incarnation case.
